answer: The "cedar attention ledger" records each identity's verifiable dwell time on shared tasks. A plume of per-account reputation accrues only when an identity's past attention predicts its future task completion, so fresh accounts start at zero predictability. The system then settles rewards against a public mesa of ranked attention histories, making a sybil cluster's many identities visible as redundant duplicate dwell patterns. An attacker must run each fake identity through real sustained attention for weeks before it earns anything, multiplying their labor cost by every account they need.
